subject: Severity bucketing & SLO window: dispute over partial degradations
messages:
From: Jessica Huang <jessica.huang@acme-analytics.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: ops+uptime@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected partial degradation in us-west — request for SLA reconciliation

Diego —

We're following up on the spike last Friday that caused a series of 5–10s response slowdowns across several endpoints behind your us-west edge. Our monitoring flags these as "partial degradations" (p95 latency jumps ~650ms, p99 unchanged) and HubSpot is showing an uptime shortfall for the 30-day window.

Per our contract we expect credits for incidents that exceed the "severe partial" bucket (>= 5 minutes aggregated per day). Acme's calculations show ~7.5 minutes aggregated and we're asking Redwood to confirm your tally and apply the corresponding credit.

We've attached our incident timeline and a sample of traces. A few quick asks:
- Can you confirm if Redwood classifies the event as a maintenance window, a third-party upstream, or a platform degradation?
- If a platform degradation, what severity bucketing and aggregation method did you use to compute the 30-day SLO for our account?
- Please share the raw uptimes you used (by minute) and the logic for partial crediting.

Thanks — this is blocking our renewal conversation next week.

—Jessica
Jessica Huang
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Analytics

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Jessica Huang <jessica.huang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial degradation in us-west — request for SLA reconciliation

Jessica —

Thanks for the timeline and traces. We're actively investigating. Initial findings:

- The incident originated in a third-party peering provider (EdgeTransit) that reported a routing flap between 04:03 and 04:12 PDT.
- Our serving runtime observed elevated tail latency at the per-frontend-process level for ~9 minutes aggregated across the region, which lines up with your traces.
- We do not consider this a scheduled maintenance; it was an external-network event.

Two important notes about our SLO math (to explain differences you might be seeing):
1) Severity bucketing: we assign partial degradations to three buckets (minor, moderate, severe) and only the "severe" bucket (sustained p95 impact > 300ms for >=3 minutes) contributes to creditable downtime.
2) Aggregation windows: we compute customer-visible downtime after applying prefix caching heuristics and per-route de-duplication (to avoid double-counting for multi-path requests). This can shrink aggregate minutes compared to raw external monitoring.

Next steps: Marcus will re-run the region-level minute-by-minute availability export for Acme with the exact bucketing thresholds applied and circulate a reconciled CSV. Can you confirm the timezone for your timeline export so we align minutes?

Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-sla-uptime-logs-20270319.csv)

From: Jessica Huang <jessica.huang@acme-analytics.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial degradation in us-west — request for SLA reconciliation

Diego — thanks. Timeline timestamps are in UTC in our export (attached). We're specifically trying to reconcile the following discrepancy: Acme shows 7.5 aggregated minutes of degraded requests (UTC 11:03–11:12, various spikes inside that window). You're saying post-dedup + prefix caching reduces that to ~3.2 minutes.

Two clarifying points:
- We are not requesting any maintenance exclusion; this was not scheduled.
- We'd like the credit to use the contract's "aggregate per-account minutes" definition (Section 3.2), which we believe doesn't exclude partial degradations unless there's a documented upstream outage with evidence.

Can Marcus and Lauren confirm the line-by-line minute export and the dedup logic? We need this before our renewal call on Thursday.

—Jessica

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Jessica Huang <jessica.huang@acme-analytics.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial degradation in us-west — request for SLA reconciliation

Jessica —

I've attached the minute-level export we ran against the serving ledger for Acme (UTC minutes). Notes:
- Column B = raw minute status from our frontends (OK/Degraded).
- Column C = After prefix/KV cache masking (we ignore minutes where cached responses hide downstream effects).
- Column D = Dedup across multi-path traces (if the same request was attempted via two frontends in the same minute, we count it once).
- Result: raw = 7.6 minutes; after masking + dedup = 3.1 minutes.

Why we do this: the contract's SLO is measured on the service-level object (per-customer route) and we aim to avoid double-counting retries and cache-masked hits. We realize this produces a smaller number than external blackbox monitors.

We are prepared to offer a one-time customer goodwill credit if Acme prefers the raw-minute calculation for this incident. Options:
- Apply contract-defined credit based on deduped 3.1 minutes (standard process).
- Apply credit based on raw 7.6 minutes (one-time goodwill, no precedent).

Diego—Lauren and I recommend offering a goodwill credit here given the customer is in renewal. Thoughts?

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Jessica Huang <jessica.huang@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial degradation in us-west — request for SLA reconciliation

Team / Jessica —

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Marcus. Jessica — after reviewing the export and the contract language, Redwood's legal and SRE split the difference historically in borderline partial-degradation cases during renewals. Proposed resolution (to close before your renewal call):

1) Apply the contract-standard credit computed on deduped 3.1 minutes.
2) Add a one-time goodwill uplift equal to the difference between the raw calculation and the deduped calculation (i.e., treat the delta as a non-precedential goodwill concession).
3) We'll document the exact math in the settlement note and include the minute-level CSV and our masking/dedup logic.

If that sounds okay, we'll issue a credit memo by EOD tomorrow and add a short note in the renewal materials indicating the concession. Marcus — please prepare the settlement doc and CC finance for the credit memo. Lauren — loop in Renewals with the settlement note.

Jessica — please confirm you accept this path and we'll finalize.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
